(Optional) Audit other Optional[str] date-like fields on Pydantic models to ensure they're listed in utils/serde.py:STRING_DATE_KEYS — pattern is fragile (silent 500s on first GET that happens to read such a field).
critical_code_review_comments: BUG (FIXED) — utils/serde.py:deserialize_datetime had no entry for 'visit_date' or 'invoice_date'. The new PatientNote.visit_date / Invoice.invoice_date fields are typed Optional[str] (YYYY-MM-DD), but deserialize_datetime parsed the stored ISO string into a datetime, causing FastAPI ResponseValidationError (500) on GET /api/patient-notes for any patient with imported notes. Root cause: utils/serde.py only excludes a hand-curated set; new string-typed dates must be added there or their first read will 500. Mitigation applied: added 'visit_date' + 'invoice_date' to STRING_DATE_KEYS. Same class of bug will recur every time a new Optional[str] date field is added — consider an alternative: rely on the Pydantic model's annotations rather than maintaining a manual allow-list (e.g. fetch model fields via get_type_hints() on insert/read paths).

imports.py:752 inserts patient_notes without `clinic_id`. The list_patient_notes router only filters by patient_id (which is itself clinic-scoped via the patient lookup), so this currently still tenant-isolates correctly — but storing clinic_id on every doc would make $regex cleanup safer and align with the rest of the schema.

DataImportTab.jsx:242 uses `new Date(row.visit_date)` for formatting — when visit_date is a YYYY-MM-DD string this works in modern Chrome/Edge, but Safari is stricter; consider `new Date(row.visit_date + 'T00:00:00')`.
PatientProfilePage.jsx:96-150 sorts events on `at` (visit_date for imported, created_at for non-imported) — correct for clinical chronology. Confirmed working via API → UI pipeline.

rca of the issue: RCA — GET /api/patient-notes 500: After Phase B added `visit_date: Optional[str]` to PatientNote model and the import path stored 'YYYY-MM-DD' strings, the read path /app/backend/routers/ref_docs.py:79 calls `deserialize_datetime(n)` on each note. utils/serde.py:deserialize_datetime is recursive and converts any ISO-like string back to datetime UNLESS the dict key is in a hand-maintained allow-list (STRING_DATE_KEYS). 'visit_date' was not in that set, so the string was coerced to a datetime; then FastAPI's response_model=List[PatientNote] validation failed with `string_type` errors at .visit_date, returning 500. Reproduction: import any CSV/XLSX that produces a patient_note with visit_date, then GET /api/patient-notes?patient_id=<that-patient> -> 500. Mitigation applied: added 'visit_date' and 'invoice_date' to STRING_DATE_KEYS. Verified via test_imported_via_surfaces_on_api_responses (now PASS). Long-term fix suggestion: replace the manual allow-list with model-driven introspection (use Pydantic model field annotations to decide which keys to keep as strings).
